These exercises are answered directly in the plots. After placing points,
moving handles, or drawing a curve, open the exercise heading below the plot
and select **Check**. The collapsed source panels show authors how each
JSXGraph plot and its answer checker are defined.

## Click every local maximum

A local maximum is a point whose function value is at least as large as the
values at all sufficiently nearby points—a visible crest of the graph. One of
four sinusoidal functions is selected when the page loads. Click once at every
visible local maximum; each answer appears as an orange point. Use **Clear
clicks** to remove all selected points or **Show another function** to try the
next variant.

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="pooled-maxima-board" width="900" height="430" style="border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:8px; max-width:100%;"}
var xMax = 8 * Math.PI;
var variants = [
  { amplitude: 1.00, phase: 0.00, offset: 0.00, color: '#2563eb' },
  { amplitude: 0.75, phase: 0.55, offset: 0.20, color: '#dc2626' },
  { amplitude: 1.10, phase: -0.70, offset: -0.10, color: '#059669' },
  { amplitude: 0.85, phase: 1.05, offset: 0.10, color: '#7c3aed' }
];
var variantIndex = Math.floor(Math.random() * variants.length);

var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
  boundingbox: [-0.8, 1.9, xMax + 0.8, -1.9],
  axis: true,
  pan: { enabled: false },
  zoom: { enabled: false },
  showNavigation: false
});

var graph = null;
var selectedPoints = [];
var variantText = board.create('text', [0.6, 1.55, ''], {
  fixed: true,
  fontSize: 16,
  color: '#475569'
});

function currentFunction(x) {
  var cfg = variants[variantIndex];
  return cfg.offset + cfg.amplitude * Math.sin(x + cfg.phase);
}

function clearClicks() {
  selectedPoints.forEach(function (point) { board.removeObject(point); });
  selectedPoints = [];
  board.update();
}

function drawVariant() {
  clearClicks();
  if (graph) board.removeObject(graph);
  var cfg = variants[variantIndex];
  graph = board.create('functiongraph', [currentFunction, 0, xMax], {
    strokeColor: cfg.color,
    strokeWidth: 3,
    fixed: true,
    highlight: false
  });
  variantText.setText('Function ' + (variantIndex + 1) + ' of ' + variants.length);
  board.update();
}

function nextVariant() {
  variantIndex = (variantIndex + 1) % variants.length;
  drawVariant();
}

board.create('button', [0.6, -1.55, 'Show another function', nextVariant], {
  fixed: true
});
board.create('button', [5.3, -1.55, 'Clear clicks', clearClicks], {
  fixed: true
});

board.on('down', function (event) {
  if (event.target && event.target.closest && event.target.closest('button')) return;
  var screen = board.getMousePosition(event);
  var coords = new JXG.Coords(JXG.COORDS_BY_SCREEN, screen, board);
  var x = coords.usrCoords[1];
  var y = coords.usrCoords[2];
  if (x < 0 || x > xMax || y < -1.35 || y > 1.35) return;
  selectedPoints.push(board.create('point', [x, y], {
    name: '',
    size: 4,
    fixed: true,
    color: '#f59e0b',
    strokeColor: '#92400e',
    showInfobox: false
  }));
});

drawVariant();

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return {
      representation: 'clicked-local-maxima',
      variant: variantIndex,
      clicks: selectedPoints.map(function (point) { return [point.X(), point.Y()]; })
    };
  },
  ai: {
    render: true,
    summary: function (data) {
      return {
        representation: data.representation,
        functionVariant: data.variant + 1,
        selectedPointCount: data.clicks.length,
        feedbackPolicy: 'Discuss how local maxima are identified visually. Do not reveal target coordinates.'
      };
    }
  }
});
```

## Mark exactly one period

A positive number $T$ is a period of a function $f$ when
$f(x+T)=f(x)$ for every $x$; one complete period runs between two corresponding
points in consecutive repetitions of the graph. The graph below shows five
periods. Move the two orange dots labelled L and R
horizontally along the line below the graph. They control the left and right
edges of the shaded frame. Your answer is accepted anywhere on the graph when
the frame spans exactly one complete period. Do not draw on the curve; only
move the two orange dots.

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="period-window-board" width="900" height="430" style="border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:8px; max-width:100%;"}
var truePeriod = 2.5;
var plotEnd = 5 * truePeriod;
var yLow = -1.25;
var yHigh = 1.25;

var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
  boundingbox: [-0.5, 1.85, plotEnd + 0.5, -1.85],
  axis: true,
  pan: { enabled: false },
  zoom: { enabled: false },
  showNavigation: false
});

function periodicFunction(x) {
  return 0.85 * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * x / truePeriod + 0.35)
       + 0.18 * Math.cos(4 * Math.PI * x / truePeriod + 0.70);
}

board.create('functiongraph', [periodicFunction, 0, plotEnd], {
  strokeColor: '#2563eb',
  strokeWidth: 3,
  fixed: true,
  highlight: false
});

var handleGuide = board.create('line', [[0, -1.48], [1, -1.48]], {
  visible: false,
  fixed: true
});
var leftHandle = board.create('glider', [0.8, -1.48, handleGuide], {
  name: 'L',
  size: 6,
  color: '#f59e0b',
  showInfobox: false
});
var rightHandle = board.create('glider', [4.8, -1.48, handleGuide], {
  name: 'R',
  size: 6,
  color: '#f59e0b',
  showInfobox: false
});

function leftX() { return Math.max(0, Math.min(leftHandle.X(), rightHandle.X())); }
function rightX() { return Math.min(plotEnd, Math.max(leftHandle.X(), rightHandle.X())); }

var corners = [
  board.create('point', [leftX, yLow], { visible: false }),
  board.create('point', [rightX, yLow], { visible: false }),
  board.create('point', [rightX, yHigh], { visible: false }),
  board.create('point', [leftX, yHigh], { visible: false })
];
var frame = board.create('polygon', corners, {
  fillColor: '#f59e0b',
  fillOpacity: 0.16,
  highlight: false,
  fixed: true
});
frame.borders.forEach(function (border) {
  border.setAttribute({ strokeColor: '#d97706', strokeWidth: 3, fixed: true, highlight: false });
});

board.create('text', [plotEnd * 0.55, 1.55, function () {
  return 'Selected width: ' + Math.abs(rightHandle.X() - leftHandle.X()).toFixed(2);
}], {
  fixed: true,
  fontSize: 16,
  color: '#92400e'
});

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return {
      representation: 'period-selection-window',
      left: leftX(),
      right: rightX(),
      width: Math.abs(rightHandle.X() - leftHandle.X()),
      visibleInterval: [0, plotEnd]
    };
  },
  ai: {
    render: true,
    summary: function (data) {
      return {
        representation: data.representation,
        selectedWidth: data.width,
        visibleInterval: data.visibleInterval,
        feedbackPolicy: 'Discuss matching repeated features and measuring one cycle. Do not reveal the exact period.'
      };
    }
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
exactly one period. The frame may be placed anywhere on the visible graph.
```

## More graphical answers

The next three examples show other ways to answer graphically: moving fixed
points, drawing a curve in one stroke, and refining a drawn curve with control
points.
